| `package.json`      | one per project, own dependencies      | one at the root, single version policy  |

Package-based keeps every project a normal npm package and adds NX on top. Integrated hands the build and test configuration to NX plugins in exchange for generators and automated migrations.

patterns: This bank is the site's best answer-shape template and should be the model in the style guide. Every card is: a heading that is itself the one-line answer ('Target = what to run, executor = how to run it', 'Workspaces manage packages, NX manages tasks', 'Same inputs → replayed result'), then a first sentence that answers directly, then bullets or a numbered pipeline, then a small commented code block, then a pitfall split across 2-3 sentences. Result: 10% of EN sentences over the limit and 2.7% of RU — against 54%/33% in cicd-devops and 52%/36% in bundlers — with no loss of depth (cache hashing, target-config layering, inferred targets and barrel-as-public-API are all covered properly).

The `**Common pitfall:**` block is still the densest text in the card, even here. 19% of its EN sentences are over the limit versus 6% in the bodies, and the longest sentence in each locale (37w EN / 34w RU, q6) sits inside it. But 0 of 12 blocks are a single sentence, which is exactly what the other two banks get wrong (6/20 in bundlers, 19/20 in cicd-devops). Whatever discipline was applied to pitfalls here is the discipline the other banks need.

Difficulty seam: not observable — all 12 questions are `junior`, so there is no boundary to break at. Worth noting the inverse: this bank proves the seam is not caused by difficulty. Its junior answers average 169 words (EN) and cover Project Crystal, target-config merge order and cache-hash inputs, i.e. genuinely middle/senior material, at 10% over-limit sentences. Depth and short sentences are not in tension; the other banks' senior tiers just weren't edited.

The residual RU defect is a thin layer of untranslated or transliterated English on top of otherwise lively Russian, and it concentrates in headings and bullet labels — the highest-visibility, lowest-word-count positions. «composition root» and «скаффолдит» are in `###` headings; «Границы, которые можно принуждать» and «Минимальный buy-in» are in bold bullet labels. The body prose around them is genuinely good («уезжает одним PR», «сползает в запутанный клубок», «CI едет час из-за однострочной правки», «не глядя»).
notes: Coverage judgement, as asked. 12 questions for a 15-chapter course is not a usable practice surface, and the gap is not uniform: the bank covers chapters 00-04, 07 and parts of 01/08, and covers them well. It has zero questions for chapter 05 (affected — mentioned in six answers, never the subject of one), 06 (libs architecture, tags, module-boundary rules — the enforcement mechanism is named four times and never explained), 09/10/11 (microfrontends, Module Federation in NX, shared-deps pitfalls — three consecutive chapters, nothing), 12 (fullstack Node API), 13 (CI and Nx Cloud — remote caching gets one sentence in q12), 14 (reading an existing workspace). Second, all 12 are `junior`, so a learner who finishes the course has no way to rehearse the material the second half of the course exists to teach; the hardest thing the bank asks is 'what does the cache store'. Concretely: the bank needs ~10-14 more questions, weighted middle/senior, and Module Federation + boundary tags + `affected` in CI are the three highest-value additions. That is a content gap, not a readability one — the 12 questions that exist are the best-written cards I audited, and the verdict `ok` refers to them.
